Description:
The most degenerate plane/torus contact that exists: the plane x = 12 touching the torus with major
radius 20 and minor radius 8 about the z axis at the SINGLE point (12, 0, 0) of its inner equator.

The inner equator is where the torus has negative Gaussian curvature and where its two principal
curvatures have opposite signs, 1/r = 1/8 along the tube and -1/(R-r) = -1/12 around the axis. A plane
tangent there therefore CROSSES the surface: the intersection curve has a NODE at (12, 0, 0), two
branches crossing at one point, and the contact is a single tangential point rather than the two of the
Villarceau case.

Everything that can coincide does coincide here, which is why the case exists:
  - the contact is at y = 0, exactly in the xz plane where the torus is split into its half faces,
  - it is at the innermost point of the tube, the extreme meridian, where the second face split of a
    torus sits,
  - and it is the point of the torus closest to its own axis, so the two branches of the intersection
    curve cross exactly on the face boundary in BOTH parameter directions.
The cutting body is a box from x = 12 to x = 52 covering the whole torus in y and z, so its face x = 12
is the tangent plane and all its other faces are far away.
Expected:
V(torus) = 2*pi^2*R*r^2 = 2*pi^2*20*64 = 2560*pi^2 = 25266.1872672626,
area 4*pi^2*R*r = 4*pi^2*160 = 6316.5468168156, extent -28,-28,-8 .. 28,28,8.
V(box) = 40*80*40 = 128000.

The part of the torus with x >= 12 has no closed form; it was integrated in cylindrical coordinates,
where the measure of the azimuth for a point of the meridian disc at distance rho from the axis is
2*acos(12/rho), giving
  V = 4 * integral over the meridian disc of rho*acos(12/rho) ... = 7352.7245
by Simpson on 1600 x 3200 points, converged to 7 digits (7352.723888 / 7352.724341 / 7352.724455 for
400x800, 800x1600, 1600x3200) and confirmed by Monte Carlo, 7356.4 +- 4.1 with 3e6 samples. So:
  tangentPlaneInter (torus and box)   7352.7245
  tangentPlaneRest  (torus minus box) 25266.1872672626 - 7352.7245 = 17913.4628
  tangentPlaneUnion 128000 + 17913.4628 = 145913.4628

The SHAPE matters more than the volume here. The plane touches the tube at the one point where the ring
is narrowest in x, so the remaining part, torus minus box, is pinched to a single point at (12, 0, 0):
the ring is cut open there without any face being removed, and the result is a body of genus 0 that is
non manifold at exactly one point. That is the correct answer, and the failure to look for is a result
that either keeps the ring closed or loses a piece of it.
The other part, the intersection, is a single solid touching the plane at that same point.
Status:
PASSES, first measured 2026-08-28, stable over 4 runs - which is the surprise of this group: the most
degenerate configuration of all of them is the one that works. The contact sits on the seam of the
torus in BOTH parameter directions at once and the plane still gets cut correctly.

  tangentPlaneInter 7352.60327988 against the integrated 7352.7245                     1.6e-5
  tangentPlaneRest  17913.2917929 against 25266.1872672626 - 7352.7245 = 17913.4628     9.5e-6
  tangentPlaneUnion 145913.327279 against 128000 + 17913.4628 = 145913.4628             9.3e-7
  inter + rest = 25265.8951 against the exact torus volume 2*pi^2*20*64 = 25266.1873    1.2e-5
and the extents are right where they have to be: the intersection reaches x = 12 exactly and the
remaining part reaches x = 12.0000000035, so both meet in the tangent plane; y = +-25.2982212813 is
sqrt(28^2 - 12^2) = sqrt(640) to the last digit.

The topology is the point of the case and it is right: tangentPlaneRest has euler 1, not 0 and not 2 -
the ring has been cut open at one single point, so its genus dropped from 1 to 0 and the body is non
manifold exactly there. tangentPlaneUnion keeps euler 0 and one hole loop, the ring is still closed
through the box. Nothing is lost and nothing is welded shut.

RE-RECORDED 2026-08-28 after the second fix of the same day. The topology of every object is
unchanged - same faces, edges, vertices, euler and surface histogram - and the volumes moved by at most
1.4e-6. One field did change: the extent of tangentPlaneInter in z, from +-7.9999410261 to
+-7.95304469067. The true value is exactly +-8, reached at the extreme meridian of the tube, so the
recorded extent got WORSE, from 7e-6 off to 6e-3 off. Since the topology is identical this is the
triangulation and not the BRep: the mesh no longer places a vertex at the extreme meridian. Worth
knowing when the extents of other cases start to drift.
